claude.sample_unit: cases (300 real-world dialogues plus 154 standardized cases)

links.outcome: Depression and suicide risk classification F1 with versus without RAG grounding in clinical knowledge base
links.effect: RAG consistently improved diagnostic performance; Qwen3 suicide risk F1 0.9548 on the Standard Case Set, about 0.15 F1 improvement over non-RAG; summary BLEU-2 up 44.1-207.2%.
links.quote: Notably, RAG integration consistently enhanced four-class severity stratification ( Fig. 3 , S2 ) : Qwen3 with RAG attained a suicide risk F1-score of 0.9548 on the Standard Case Set, substantially outperforming its non-RAG counterpart (ΔF1 ≈ 0.15 improvement) (Fig. S2 C).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of diagnostic and suicide risk outputs across 10 repeated runs of 30 transcripts
links.effect: Overall consistency kappa 0.93 (95% CI 0.91-0.95); diagnostic classification kappa 0.97; risk level kappa 0.97; symptom description kappa 0.86.
links.quote: The overall consistency index (κ = 0.93, SD = 0.04, 95% CI: 0.91–0.95) further confirms the system’s stability across repeated assessments ( Table 1 ).

links.outcome: Reference standard creation with independent annotators and senior adjudication
links.effect: Two board-certified psychiatrists independently annotated all cases, with discrepancies resolved by a third senior psychiatrist; ICC(2,1)=0.85 for ratings by blinded psychiatrists.
links.quote: Any diagnostic discrepancies were resolved through a final review by a third, senior psychiatrist to reach a definitive consensus.

unlisted_practices: On-premises local deployment of LLM and knowledge base for privacy
Hybrid retrieval with keyword re-ranking prioritizing suicide-related content
Mandatory human-in-the-loop verification before suicide-risk alerts are sent (proposed, not tested)

links.effect: Qwen3 + RAG suicide risk F1-score 0.9548; ΔF1 ≈ 0.15 versus non-RAG.
links.quote: Notably, RAG integration consistently enhanced four-class severity stratification ( Fig. 3 , S2 ) : Qwen3 with RAG attained a suicide risk F1-score of 0.9548 on the Standard Case Set, substantially outperforming its non-RAG counterpart (ΔF1 ≈ 0.15 improvement) (Fig. S2 C).
The overall consistency index (κ = 0.93, SD = 0.04, 95% CI: 0.91–0.95) further confirms the system’s stability across repeated assessments ( Table 1 ).

links.effect: Qwen3 + RAG F1-scores: 0.94 no risk, 0.80 low, 0.74 moderate, 0.83 high.
links.quote: For suicide risk four-class classification on the Hao Daifu dataset, the Qwen3 + RAG model achieved F1-scores of 0.94 (no risk), 0.80 (low risk), 0.74 (moderate risk), and 0.83 (high risk).

links.effect: Base empathy scores 3.20–3.80; RAG mean scores increased to 4.23–4.98/5.
links.quote: Base configurations without clinical knowledge retrieval demonstrated moderate empathy scores, ranging from 3.20 to 3.80 across emotional matching, dialogue consistency, and care expression domains.

links.outcome: suicide risk and depression classification accuracy
links.effect: RAG-enhanced Qwen3 model suicide risk classification F1-score was 0.15 higher than non-RAG version
links.quote: Notably, the F1-score of the RAG-enhanced Qwen3 model for suicide risk classification was 0.15 higher than that of its non-RAG version.
